title: Want it to stick? Say it out loud
teaser: In a 2010 study, students recognised 76% of the words they had read aloud and 60% of the ones they had read silently. The catch: it only worked when some words stayed silent.

slides.alt: Reel cover: Memory Lab. Want it to stick? Say it out loud.

body: Want it to stick? Say it out loud.

In a 2010 study, 44 students read one list of words: blue words aloud, white words silently. On a recognition test afterwards, they said yes to 76% of the words they had read aloud and 60% of the ones they had read silently.

The researchers' explanation is distinctiveness: saying a word gives it something extra to remember, which a silent word doesn't have. That's also the catch. When one group read every word aloud and another read every word silently, the advantage on the same kind of test disappeared.
Send this to someone studying tonight.
forDesigners: Ask learners to say, not just read, the one or two lines that matter most. Make everything loud and nothing stands out.

sources.label: MacLeod, C.M., Gopie, N., Hourihan, K.L., Neary, K.R. & Ozubko, J.D. (2010). The production effect: Delineation of a phenomenon. Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition, 36(3), 671–685. Experiments 1A and 1B, Table 1; Experiment 2.
